raceFix.cgo: -race needs cgo and this pod has CGO_ENABLED=0 by default: a plain `go test -race` exits 2 with `-race requires cgo; enable cgo by setting CGO_ENABLED=1`. gcc IS present (/usr/bin/gcc), so CGO_ENABLED=1 makes it work. Worth knowing for anyone reading a -race run in a pod: without that variable the run reports no races because it never ran.

proof.criterion: A listener SIGKILLed mid-handover with copies left and a live holder is recovered by the restart sweep: every copy reaches the holder, with no new claim.
proof.surface: A real envoy-listener process built from this head on a real NATS server with a real session process on a serving port; 40 copies kept, the role claimed, the listener SIGKILLed part way and restarted under the same machine id.
proof.observed: Killed with 6 of 40 delivered and the holder still live. The restarted listener finished the lane with no new claim: 40 of 40. One copy was delivered twice, and its two deliveries carry ONE dedupe key on the bus, so the holder drops the repeat — the design's accepted worst case, never a loss. An earlier run of the same rig delivered 40 of 40 with no repeat at all.
proof.negativeControl: Round 6's mutation of the sweep (handing over nothing) fails TestTheSweepHandsOverALaneNoHandoverIsDraining; and restarting under a DIFFERENT machine id, which I measured in round 6, delivers only a part of the lane, because a serving-port holder is not served by another machine's listener — which is why this rig reuses the machine id.

findings.why it is sound: That test asserted the outbox's role envelope carries no keep key. With `keep` deleted from the envelope contract, the schema and the Go mirror, the publisher cannot carry one: the property is now enforced by the type rather than by an assertion, and the publisher's own change this round is comment-only (I read the diff: the whole of publisher.go's change is the doc comment above publishRoute). The behaviour it protected is still covered twice — the listener-side TestADispatchRoleRoutedEventToAnUnheldRoleReachesTheNextHolder, which passes, and my live section C. I record the deletion because a reviewer counting tests would otherwise see a pinned behaviour lose its test.
